description:
Found while building String.Chars for fz-5xp.15.

    fnp kind(s :: binary), do: {:binary, s}
    fnp kind(_other), do: :not_a_binary

    kind(<<1::4>>)   ->  {:binary, <<1::4>>}    on all three doors

A four-bit bitstring satisfies a `:: binary` clause head. Elixir distinguishes
`binary()` (byte-aligned) from `bitstring()`, and `is_binary/1` is false for
`<<1::4>>`.

This matters because fz deliberately replaced Elixir's `is_*` guards with
type-annotated clause heads. That substitution is exact for `integer`, `float`,
`atom` and the rest -- but for binaries it silently widens, and the annotation
that reads like `is_binary(x)` behaves like `is_bitstring(x)`.

CONSEQUENCE, already hit: `String.Chars` promises `:: binary` and Elixir guards
its BitString impl with `is_binary`. fz's impl could not express the guard and
had to call a runtime predicate (`fz_bitstring_is_binary`) instead. Without it
the impl returned a partial bitstring as a `binary`, and the damage surfaced at
the next `<>` as a byte-alignment abort inside `fz_binary_concat` -- far from
the call that was actually wrong.

DONE = `binary` means byte-aligned, with `bitstring` available for the wider
type, so a `:: binary` clause head rejects `<<1::4>>` on all three doors and
`String.Chars.Binary` can drop its runtime predicate. Check the other places
`binary` is used as a bound while in there -- the extern wire type `binary`
already assumes byte alignment (`byte_aligned_binary_slice` asserts it), so
they may be the same fix.
title: [BUG] fz's binary type does not exclude a non-byte-aligned bitstring
